summary: The three routed findings are fixed and the live read works: quota.ts reads the weekly key (F1), skips a null, non-number, or negative window and stops only when no usable window is left (F2), the spec D15 example and doc comment hold the live keys (N3), and the live read at 127.0.0.1:38307 gives state ready on the live window set with the null credits_balance skipped. All four suites pass one file at a time (quota 24, review-run 53, judge-run 30, adversarial 14, all exit 0) and the plan evidence of rows 4.13g-4.13j matches what I reproduced, including the Red record red-4.13i.txt. Green decision (a) N1 is accepted: both runners now key the Go rule, the quota read, and the credential seed on quota_provider, the one field quota.ts reads, so the rule cannot disagree with the read, and a bogus provider fails closed. But Green decision (b) B2 is a blocker: the Go required-window check at quota.ts:319-324 keys on raw window names (answer.names, built at quota.ts:273) instead of usable values, so a Go answer whose weekly window is present but unusable (null, a string, or negative) gives ready beside a usable 5h. I reproduced this against the real binary: weekly null, -1, and "10" beside 5h 50 all give state ready. Plan row 4.13j orders "both 5h and weekly must be finite numbers, else stopped", and Review B cc8afbd B2 names this exact fail-open (a partial or damaged answer starts a Go pass, probe, or judge call). Q13 pins the unsafe behavior as correct (quota.test.ts:648-662). The night driver night-4.11.sh:83-87 and the probe probe-4.10.sh:68-72 both refuse a Go route when 5h or weekly is not usable, so the readers of the same source disagree with quota.ts. Two cross-session events contaminated my first runs (a sibling monitor shell whose command text contains the scan strings, and sibling leftover fake servers); clean re-runs pass with empty pgrep scans.

blocking_findings.finding: The Go required-window check keys on raw window names, not usable values: main() tests answer.names.has("5h") and answer.names.has("weekly"), and answer.names (built at quota.ts:273) holds every window name, usable or not. So an opencode-go answer whose weekly window is present but unusable gives ready beside a usable 5h. Reproduced against the real binary with a loopback fake: weekly usedPercent null, -1, and "10" beside 5h 50 and monthly 10 all give {"state":"ready","windows":{"5h":50,"monthly":10}} with no weekly value at all. The runner trusts only the state, so a damaged or shape-changed Go answer starts a pass, a probe, or a judge call with no verified week budget (fail open). Plan row 4.13j (measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md:2285-2287) orders: "B2: for opencode-go, both 5h and weekly must be finite numbers, else stopped" — null and a string are not finite numbers, and N2 of the same row makes -1 unusable, so the ordered rule gives stopped where the code gives ready. Review B cc8afbd B2 names this exact effect. Q13 (harness/model-guide-tests/quota.test.ts:648-662) pins the unsafe behavior: expectState(negative, "ready", "negative beside usable windows") for weekly -1 beside a usable 5h, and the same code path gives ready for a null weekly, unpinned by any test. The night driver night-4.11.sh:83-87 and the probe probe-4.10.sh:68-72 both treat a not-usable 5h or weekly as a failure and skip the route, so the readers of the same source disagree. Green's own plan evidence (plan.md:2298-2300) discloses the narrowing ("a present but unusable window is skipped, as Q13 pins"), which contradicts the row's own directive.
blocking_findings.fix: In quota.ts main(), require both Go windows in the usable set instead of the name set: check GO_FIVEH_WINDOW and GO_WEEK_WINDOW in answer.windows (drop the names set or keep it only for a distinct stop reason), so a present but unusable 5h or weekly gives stopped. Flip Q13's negative-weekly sub-case to expectStopped and add a case with weekly null beside a usable 5h -> stopped. The live read is unaffected: the live 5h and weekly are usable numbers. Add the same required-window wording to the D15 sentence (spec.md:749-750) so the spec names usability, not just name presence, and fix FR-15 in the same pass (see N4).

nonblocking_findings.finding: Carried from review-a-cc8afbd: the comment at lines 671-673 still says a window of 70 % or more stops the run and a window of 80 % or more stops it after the previous group, but the wait branch at line 684 stops the run at 70 first, so the QUOTA_MAX >= 80 branch at line 692 is dead for every sourced route. The new IS_GO_ROUTE guard keeps the dead branch. Pre-existing, no behavior change from this range.
nonblocking_findings.fix: Either drop the dead branch or fix the comment to say the wait state covers it. No behavior change is needed.

nonblocking_findings.finding: FR-15 still says the tool gives stopped "for a source with no value, a missing field, or a value that is not a number", but the rewritten D15 (spec.md:746-750) and the pinned behavior skip such a window and stop only when no usable window is left. Q12 and Q14 pin the skip on kimi and Go. The spec contradicts itself between D15 and FR-15 after this range rewrote only D15.
nonblocking_findings.fix: Update the FR-15 sentence to the D15 wording (skip an unusable window; stop when no usable window is left; for Go, stop when 5h or weekly is absent or unusable) when Green fixes F3.

nonblocking_findings.finding: The liveness and orphan scans match any command line whose text contains "fake-opencode", "quota-server", or "mg-". A sibling session's monitor shell (PID 2510184, `bash -c sleep 120; uptime; pgrep -af 'mg-review-run|mg-judge-run|fake-opencode|quota-server' ...`) made review-run's afterAll fail once and judge-run fail three checks (J14, J14b, and the suite afterAll) without any defect in the code under review; both suites pass with empty scans once the monitor exits. Under the same load, review-run P4 failed once on a real liveness race (two fake processes inside my own fixture tree still alive at the assertion; both died right after). All three resolved on clean re-runs. Pre-existing pattern, but the gates are fragile on this shared machine.
nonblocking_findings.fix: Filter the scan matches to the run's own temp tree (the fixture repo path) instead of any line that mentions "mg-", and give P4's liveness check a short retry window. No behavior change.

evidence: F1 fixed: quota.ts:68 sets GO_WEEK_WINDOW = "weekly" and stateOf reads windows["weekly"] (quota.ts:291). Every fake that serves opencode-go now uses the live set "5h", "weekly", "monthly", plus a null credits_balance: quota.test.ts (Q11, and the Q9/Q10 label assertions read ["weekly"]), review-run.test.ts:506-517 (live set on /opencode-go paths), judge-run.test.ts:547-559, adversarial-p4-runner.test.ts:186-193.

F2 fixed: parseAnswer (quota.ts:272-281) skips a window whose usedPercent is null, not a number, or negative, and stops with "the quota answer holds no usable window" only when none is left. Q12 pins the null skip and the all-null stop; Q13 pins the string skip and the only-window stop.
N3 fixed: spec D15 (spec.md:746-750) names the live windows and the null credits_balance, and the quota.ts doc comment (lines 30-43) matches.

Live read works: `cd harness && npx tsx model-guide/quota.ts --provider opencode-go --base http://127.0.0.1:38307` gives {"state":"ready","windows":{"5h":5.43,"weekly":2.17,"monthly":1.09}} (read-only GET, values rounded here). The null credits_balance window is skipped and the read gives ready, so the F2 break of the last review is gone. The plan row 4.13j live claim (ready, live window set) matches.

F3 reproduction (loopback fake, real binary, no driver, no opencode CLI): opencode-go answers with 5h 50, monthly 10, and weekly usedPercent null, -1, and "10" each give {"state":"ready","windows":{"5h":50,"monthly":10}}, exit 0, no stderr line. The live-shape control (weekly 97, null credits_balance) gives ready with weekly 97. The required-window check passed on the name "weekly" while the emitted windows hold no weekly value.

Green decision (a) N1 accepted: review-run.sh:256-264 and judge-run.sh:238-247 key the Go rule on QUOTA_PROVIDER; the quota read runs `quota.ts --provider "$QUOTA_PROVIDER"` (review-run.sh:459, judge-run.sh:312) and the credential seed uses the same field (review-run.sh:571, judge-run.sh:355-356), so the rule, the read, and the source id all derive from one field and cannot disagree. quota.ts:304 refuses a provider outside the spec D15 table (exit 2), which read_quota turns into stopped, so a bad row fails closed. routes.json holds quota_provider = quota_source on every sourced row today. The residual QUOTA_SOURCE use (one-pass-per-night guard, review-run.sh:437) is the stricter direction on a mismatch.

Driver agreement (read-only, never run): night-4.11.sh:74-87 reads windows["5h"] and windows["weekly"], stops at five >= 95 or week >= 100, and marks the route skipped when either value is not usable. probe-4.10.sh:59-73 does the same and comments "the 'weekly' key of the quota answer". My earlier N2 (probe stricter at week > 90) is withdrawn as fixed: both drivers now use >= 95 and >= 100. The remaining disagreement is F3: both drivers fail closed on an unusable weekly while quota.ts gives ready.

Red record verified: measure/runs/model_guide/red-4.13i.txt holds the live shape (no "week" or "day" key), the failing-first runs (quota 7 failed | 17 passed, review-run 52 pass 1 fail with G4), and the named reasons (F1, F2, B2). The conversion evidence matches the plan row 4.13i.

All four suites pass at HEAD e9e7d36, one file at a time, fakes only: quota.test.ts Tests 24 passed (24) exit 0; review-run.test.ts 53 pass 0 fail exit 0 (bun); judge-run.test.ts Tests 30 passed (30) exit 0; adversarial-p4-runner.test.ts Tests 14 passed (14) exit 0. Plan rows 4.13h and 4.13j claim 17/52/30/14 at 94fef2f and 24/53/30/14 at 34d6be2; I reproduced the 4.13j counts at HEAD.

Cross-session contamination, reported per the brief: (i) during my quota run a leftover /tmp/mg-review-fake-GbsG66/quota-server.js (the review-run suite prefix, which I had not yet run) belonged to a sibling session and died on its own; (ii) a sibling monitor shell (PID 2510184, `sleep 120; ... pgrep -af 'mg-review-run|mg-judge-run|fake-opencode|quota-server' ...`) tripped review-run's afterAll once and judge-run's J14, J14b, and afterAll once each, because its own command text contains the scan strings; I waited for it to exit and re-ran both suites clean; (iii) after my last review-run run a sibling /tmp/mg-judge-fake-KldGuV/quota-server.js line appeared (the judge-suite prefix; my judge run had already ended with empty scans). My own runs left nothing: each clean run's pgrep scans printed nothing beyond these cross-session lines.

HEAD is e9e7d366719e3b00ad27c299809772e72941fd70 and equals the audited head.

Vacuous-pass check (A4): expectState and expectStopped (quota.test.ts:419-433) assert the state, the exit code, and one stderr line that starts with "quota:"; Q15's day-only case asserts stopped through expectStopped, so a missing deliverable cannot pass. Count assertions are labeled integer parses, not bare-digit matches (A3). Plan claims match the actual exits (A5): rows 4.13g-4.13j hold the counts and commands I reproduced above.

Plan row 4.13j orders stopped ("both 5h and weekly must be finite numbers, else stopped"), Review B cc8afbd B2 names the fail-open, Q13 pins the unsafe behavior, and the night driver and the probe refuse the same answer, so the readers of the quota source disagree.

ratings.evidence: The live read and all gates pass (live state ready at 127.0.0.1:38307; 24/53/30/14 suites exit 0), but the Go required-window rule fails open on an unusable weekly: my loopback reproduction gives state ready for weekly null, -1, and "10" beside a usable 5h.
